top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B010) rewards one identifiable discovery. Melitz (2003) introduced firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extended it to exporting versus foreign investment. The predictions on exporter selection, exporter premia, entry and exit, and within-industry reallocation are ones that representative-firm new trade theory does not generate. Over twenty years of firm-level data from many countries have tested them, so the work is mature and its credit line is short. This matches how I judge contracting theory: a sharp mechanism that has repeatedly met real data. I moved from B019 in round 2 because B010's evidence base is more direct. B019's amplification channel is identified more indirectly, and it sits thematically close to the 2022 prize. I rank no award second because the achievement is substantial and mature, so I see no merit-based reason to withhold the prize. The citation should stay narrow, on selection, reallocation and foreign investment. It should not state welfare magnitudes, since those depend on distributional assumptions. The scientific background should acknowledge the Bernard-Jensen exporter facts, Eaton-Kortum and Hopenhayn, and Redding's later quantitative and spatial work should not be treated as co-core. The omission of those precursors is a real cost that wording only partly repairs. The slate offers only this proposal and no award, so the ranking is a straightforward choice between them.
